verdict.rationale: Browserbase offers programmatic control of real browser sessions with network interception ([browserbase-docs-1], [browserbase-docs-4]) and markets authenticated access, saying agents get past "login walls" and login prompts are "handled" ([browserbase-docs-8], [browserbase-docs-10]). This suggests a developer could reach authenticated pages, but the evidence never documents supplying your own session cookies, and the URL-fetch feature ([browserbase-docs-3]) is not shown to accept cookies. Missing for 10: documented cookie injection for sessions or the fetch API, cookie or context persistence details, and independent or hands-on corroboration of authenticated fetching.
